question: Where are MCP client/server descriptors and trust, SDK custom tools/hooks, executable/string handleSteps bundling and isolation, declarative agents/plugins, local .agents CLI wrappers, capability discovery and third-party integration actually wired?

selectedFiles.reason: Out-of-band MCP origin registry, no-upgrade and propagation rules, unknown-origin resolution and migration diagnostics. Trace local/user versus client provenance across parse/clone boundaries; process env/egress mechanics belong to pair09.

Actual tools/list cache and tools/call result projection: argument-specific discovery identity, rejection retry, text/image/audio/resource/resource-link fallback. Inspect pagination/change notifications and preservation of isError, structuredContent and content semantics at real consumers.

Production MCP discovery producer: declared server/tool selectors, provider-compatible names, concurrent per-server loading, client-origin descriptor labeling and intact server JSON schemas. Trace granted-tool semantics and partial loading, rather than treating configured membership as a grant.

Real Openbuff MCP server registry, annotations, optional mutation tool, host/index/memory seams, public structural handle and listed result shape. Compare advertised abilities with the dispatch below and actual CLI bindings.

Server-side MCP request schema and actual tools/list/tools/call dispatch, unknown-tool refusal, handler error translation, lazy mutation authority and stdio close/abort bridge. This proves external-host wiring; broker internals and process teardown are adjacent pairs.

Actual MCP/custom-tool consumer: client-origin per-run approval bookkeeping and no-approver behavior, MCP output/error conversion, original Zod async/default/transform validation and custom execute cancellation, then native override selection. Inspect callback contracts and first-party versus protocol-peer trust without duplicating generic terminal policy.

SDK agent/function serialization and custom-tool Zod-to-input-JSON-Schema projection into SessionState. Compare declared schema, provider schema and the original execution schema; track loss of closures, transforms/refinements and provenance.

Programmatic execution entry: iteration bound, string materialization provenance allowlist including the legacy undefined case, host-realm new Function, actual generator context/config injection, STEP/STEP_ALL state and yielded-value validation. Compare first-party host modules with the promised untrusted isolate/bundle path.

Programmatic callback/state projection, context-management allowlist, declared visible/hidden tool grant check and real single-tool dispatch/history/replay boundary. Focus on extension ABI and permissions; durable replay correctness belongs to pair05.

Complete executable local loader: explicit project/parent trust opt-in, supported extensions, recursive walk exclusions, import-before-definition-validation, precedence, source links, provenance and MCP origin stamps, diagnostics and lexical import containment. Explicitly inspect .agents/sessions, probes, __tests__, lib/types, node_modules and test filename variants against the actual walker.

Current agent input-schema conversion, live/degraded Zod detection, representability/fallback policy, runtime schema coercion and JSON-safe schema/function transport. Trace validation strictness and fallback reporting across bundled/local/database/supervised definitions.

Canonical published JSON-Schema and generated TypeScript tool contracts: shared provider-schema resolution, supported composite/tuple/record shapes and fail-loud unsupported shapes. Use generator consumers and tests below to assess interoperability, not just existence of generated files.

Real repository-local external CLI template: factory settings, two-phase serialized generator, tmux startup/result parsing, failure receipt, STEP_ALL and teardown, custom review flow. Inspect operation/output contracts and reliance on repository helper scripts; generic child sandbox/kill policy is pair09.

Shared external CLI wrapper prompts and workflows consumed by Codex/Claude/Gemini/local wrappers: session/capture evidence, task-file recipe, review/work modes and output/permission claims. Compare these claims with actual templates, helper scripts and intentional current profile policy.

Shared local-wrapper factory: input/config vocabulary, declared tool grants, structured output, static template/profile fields and prompt assembly. Compare the returned definition with each wrapper's independent serialized handleSteps.

Existing execution-boundary tests for defaults/transforms, asynchronous rejection, cancellation during validation and legacy direct JSON-Schema dispatch. Read only; distinguish helper coverage from full client/provider/serialization integration.

Existing host-realm programmatic tests, generator error output and explicit host-global visibility probe. Compare documented sandbox guarantees with this tested behavior and the separate provenance-guard tests; do not run probes.

Current user-facing agent-extension, secure-sandbox, declared-tool, local-loading/precedence and supported-module-format claims. Treat documentation as a contract to compare with production loading and host-realm execution, not assurance.

searchCoverage.policyContext: Parent established intentional first-party full-access execution and current relaxed/keep policy. Trusted host-realm code is not itself a defect; assess untrusted executable boundaries, actual opted-in guarantees and truthful documentation/outputs separately. Do not prescribe restrictions against that preference.
excluded: No source edits, tests/probes/process launches, API calls, credential values, private configuration values or raw session logs.
Pair09 owns generic subprocess/env/kill/approval/sandbox/egress policy; this pair owns extension trust, descriptors and callback/tool contracts.
Pair03/05 own generic orchestration and durable replay semantics; selected generator ranges here cover the extension ABI and trusted/untrusted execution boundary.
Pair06 owns physical mutation broker/receipt authority; MCP optional mutation exposure is a public extension contract edge.
Pair07/08 own language-target and indexer implementation; capability/schema/extension discovery and truthful advertisements are inspected here.
Pair11 owns overall release/distribution and dependency provenance; only extension dependency/type-generator adoption is selected.
General serving/auth/socket protocol lifecycle belongs to its pair; selected ACP slices cover peer MCP ingestion, transport conversion and extension/capability negotiation.
